analysis.title: Better Than the Tape Suggests; Subs Mix and Earnings Power Matter
key_insights: Snap's 3Q26 advertising revenue was below expectations at $1,373mn (+4.3% y/y vs DB est $1,403mn), with the softness mostly isolated to Brand, now a smaller part of the mix. Total revenue growth slowed to 14% y/y from 19% in 2Q.
The y/y comparison was roughly 15 points tougher, and 2Q benefited from World Cup-related advertiser spending and engagement.
Adjusted EBITDA was $383mn, up 110% y/y, at a 22% margin. About 93% of incremental revenue flowed through to EBITDA.
DB lowers revenue expectations modestly and raises EBITDA dollars and margins. The $8 price target and Buy rating are unchanged.

Upper-funnel brand advertising declined y/y, driven mainly by lower CPG spending amid macro pressure in the US and Middle East. DB sees early reasons for optimism into 2027: better growth in US financial services and new inventory across Chat, Spotlight and Map.

DB is not underwriting a rapid brand recovery, but says stabilization would be incrementally supportive. Direct response (DR) is now about 77% of advertising revenue, which reduces dependence on brand.

DR performance: app-purchase campaign volume more than doubled y/y, cost per purchase fell ~24% and related revenue rose 54%+. Web purchases grew 31%+, with cost per purchase down 15% and revenue up 11%.

AI-enabled product matching (Dynamic Product Ads, generative retrieval, agentic recommendations) has driven a 2.5%+ increase in pixel purchase conversions. Sponsored Snaps in Chat grew revenue 56% sequentially in 3Q.

Other (subscription) revenue grew 84% y/y, the third straight quarter above 80%. Paid subscribers across Snapchat+, Memories Storage and Lens+ passed 30mn, about 3% penetration of a monthly audience near 1bn.

Snap moves from DAU to global MAU reporting starting 1Q27 (3Q MAU 977mn), and will use MAU-based ARPU and FCF/share as its primary scorecard. It will also cut paid acquisition in markets with weak monetization economics.
4Q guidance: revenue $1.95bn-$1.99bn (~14%-16% y/y, in line with DB's $1.97bn) and Adj EBITDA $490mn-$525mn (25.1%-26.4% margin). DB raises its 4Q EBITDA estimate to $514mn from $491mn.

DB's FY26/FY27 revenue estimates are $4.05bn/$4.72bn per the text, while the tables show $6,822mn/$7,684mn. Adj EBITDA estimates rise to $1.38bn/$1.71bn from $1.32bn/$1.69bn. The $8 PT is based on 10x FY27 EV/Adj. EBITDA.
3Q26 gross margin was 62.3% vs DB's 59.8%, and FCF was $164mn vs DB's $53mn. DAUs of 495mn were slightly below DB's 497mn.

market_movers.rationale: Ad softness was isolated to Brand, while DR and subscriptions are growing and EBITDA is above estimates. DB raises EBITDA estimates and keeps the $8 PT, based on 10x FY27 EV/Adj. EBITDA.

earnings_insights: SNAP 3Q26 reported 11/2026: total revenue $1,722mn (+14.3% y/y), vs DB est $1,740mn and Street $1,731mn, and vs company guidance of $1.70-$1.74bn.
SNAP 3Q26 reported advertising revenue $1,373mn (+4.3% y/y) vs DB est $1,403mn and Street $1,396mn. Subscription (Other) revenue was $350mn (+84% y/y) vs DB est $338mn.
SNAP 3Q26 reported Adj EBITDA $383mn (22.2% margin) vs DB est $350mn, Street $338mn and guidance of $300-$350mn. Reported diluted EPS was $0.03 vs DB est $(0.01) and Street $0.01.
SNAP 4Q26 guidance: revenue $1.95bn-$1.99bn and Adj EBITDA $490mn-$525mn. DB estimates (new) are revenue $1,972mn, Adj EBITDA $514mn, EPS $0.09, vs Street $1,968mn, $516mn and $0.10.
SNAP 1Q27 DB estimates: revenue $1,736mn (prior $1,717mn), Adj EBITDA $315mn, EPS $0.00. Street is revenue $1,715mn and Adj EBITDA $317mn.
DB FY26E revenue $6,822mn (prior $6,839mn), Adj EBITDA $1,379mn (prior $1,324mn), EPS $(0.01) (prior $(0.07)). DB FY27E revenue $7,684mn, Adj EBITDA $1,708mn, EPS $0.18 (Street $0.16).
risk_factors: Brand advertising remains weak, and DB is not underwriting a rapid recovery.
Tougher y/y comparisons and the fade of World Cup-related ad spending in 2Q slowed the sequential trend.
The post-close share reaction was negative, which DB says understates the earnings trajectory.
geopolitical: Macro pressure in the US and Middle East reduced CPG brand advertising spend, per the report.

tension_points.bull_case: DR is about 77% of ad revenue and growing robustly, subscriptions grew 84% y/y at high margin, and EBITDA flow-through was ~93%. DB sees the earnings trajectory as considerably better than the post-close reaction suggests.
tension_points.bear_case: Advertising grew only 4% y/y, missing DB and Street estimates. Brand ad spend fell on lower CPG spending amid US and Middle East macro pressure, and DB is not underwriting a rapid brand recovery.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Brand stabilization would support the narrative, and continued brand declines would weigh on it. The report gives no specific level.

theme_stances.key_argument: Subscriptions and direct response are becoming a larger, higher-margin part of Snap's revenue, which makes earnings more durable than the headline ad deceleration suggests.
theme_stances.evidence: we think this remains underappreciated by investors
